newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean won closes lower on late dollar build-up.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean won closes lower on late dollar build-up.

text.p: The South Korean won closed lower against the dollar on Friday on late dollar build-up by some banks, dealers said.
The won opened firmer on expectations the inflow of foreign funds will grow early next month, but a sharp fall in the U.S. unit later sparked buying, they said.
It closed at the day's low 893.50, down from Thursday's 892.50 after reaching a high of 888.50.
"Several banks built up dollars after it fell sharply in the morning," said a foreign bank dealer. "But the dollar's rise was limited as the market is still flush with dollars."
Dollar inflows are expected to grow once the foreign shareholding limit is raised to 23 percent of a listed company on May 1 from the current 20 percent.
But dealers said many traders doubted the dollar would fall sharply in the near future.
The won's base mid-rate was forecast to be pegged at 890.50 on Monday, against 894.00 on Friday.
